Class Polygon

Namespace
ShapeEngine.Geometry.PolygonDef
Assembly
ShapeEngine.dll

Represents a 2D polygon defined by a sequence of points in counter-clockwise order, providing geometric operations, containment and intersection tests, convex hull computation, triangulation, randomization, and shape manipulation utilities.

Remarks

Points should be provided in CCW order for correct geometric calculations. Use FixWindingOrder() or MakeCounterClockwise() if your points are in clockwise (CW) order.

  • A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward."
  • A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex.

CalculatePolygonMaxLineThickness(float)

Calculates the maximum line thickness that can be safely used to draw the outline of a polygon without causing self-intersections or rendering artifacts. The result is scaled by the given safety margin factor.

Parameters

Returns

float

The maximum safe line thickness for the polygon, or 0 if the polygon is invalid.

ClipUnion(Polygon, float, Polygon)

Attempts to union this polygon with other by first bridging nearby shapes when they are within distanceThreshold.

Parameters

other Polygon

distanceThreshold float

The maximum allowed distance between the polygons before a temporary bridge polygon is generated.

result Polygon

The destination polygon that receives the union result.

Returns

bool

true if a bridge polygon was generated and the union succeeded; otherwise, false.

Remarks

This overload is intended for shapes that are close but not yet touching. It generates a temporary polygon at the closest point before performing the union.

DrawGappedOutline(float, LineDrawingInfo, GappedOutlineDrawingInfo)

Draws a gapped outline for a polygon, creating a dashed or segmented effect along the polygon's perimeter.

public float DrawGappedOutline(float perimeter, LineDrawingInfo lineInfo, GappedOutlineDrawingInfo gapDrawingInfo)

Parameters

perimeter float

The total length of the polygon's perimeter. If zero or negative, the method calculates it automatically. Providing a known length avoids redundant calculations and improves performance, especially for static segments.

lineInfo LineDrawingInfo

Parameters describing how to draw the outline.

gapDrawingInfo GappedOutlineDrawingInfo

Parameters describing the gap configuration.

Returns

float

The perimeter of the polygon if positive; otherwise, -1. If the shape does not change, the valid length can be reused in subsequent frames to avoid recalculating.

Remarks

  • If gapDrawingInfo.Gaps.Gaps is 0 or gapDrawingInfo.GapPerimeterPercentage.GapPerimeterPercentage is 0, the outline is drawn solid.
  • If gapDrawingInfo.GapPerimeterPercentage.GapPerimeterPercentage is 1 or greater, no outline is drawn.

DrawGlow(ValueRange, ValueRangeColor, int, float, bool, bool)

Draws the polygon outline as a layered glow by rendering multiple outline passes with interpolated thickness and color values.

Parameters

thicknessRange ValueRange

The outline thickness range used from the first pass to the final pass.

Generate(Segment, Polygon, float, float, float, float)

Generates a polygonal shape around the specified segment and appends its vertices to result.

public static bool Generate(Segment segment, Polygon result, float magMin = 0.1, float magMax = 0.25, float minSectionLength = 0.025, float maxSectionLength = 0.1)

Parameters

segment Segment

The segment to build a polygon around.

result Polygon

The destination polygon that receives the generated vertices.

magMin float

The minimum perpendicular offset magnitude used for intermediate points on either side of the segment.

magMax float

The maximum perpendicular offset magnitude used for intermediate points on either side of the segment.

minSectionLength float

The minimum step size along the segment, expressed as a fraction of the segment length.

maxSectionLength float

The maximum step size along the segment, expressed as a fraction of the segment length.

Returns

bool

true if the segment and generation parameters are valid and vertices were added; otherwise, false.

Remarks

The generated vertex order starts at Start, progresses toward End along one side of the segment, then returns along the opposite side. If the minimum values are greater than the corresponding maximum values, the pairs are swapped. This method does not clear result before adding vertices.

GetBoundingCircleSimple()

Returns a simple (non-minimal) enclosing circle for the polygon. You should always use GetBoundingCircle() unless performance is critical.

public Circle GetBoundingCircleSimple()

Returns

Circle

A Circle centered at the polygon centroid with radius equal to the maximum distance from the centroid to any vertex. For an empty polygon an empty Circle is returned.

This method computes an approximate bounding circle using the polygon's centroid and the maximum distance from that centroid to any vertex. It is faster (by a very small amount) than computing the minimal enclosing circle but may produce a larger-than-necessary radius. Use GetBoundingCircle() for the minimal enclosing circle.

GetEdgeNormals()

Computes and returns the normal vectors for the polygon edges.

public List<Vector2> GetEdgeNormals()

Returns

List<Vector2>

A List<T> containing one normal per edge:

  • If the polygon has 0 or 1 vertex an empty list is returned.
  • If the polygon has 2 vertices a single normal for the segment is returned.
  • For 3+ vertices returns normals for every edge (edge from vertex i to i+1).

Remarks

Normals are computed using GetNormal(Vector2, Vector2, bool) with the third parameter set to false. If the polygon points are in counter-clockwise (CCW) order the normals will face outward.

Returns

int

The number of normals added:

  • 0 when the polygon has 0 or 1 vertex (nothing is added).
  • 1 when the polygon has exactly 2 vertices (a single segment normal is added).
  • Count when the polygon has 3 or more vertices (one normal per edge).

Remarks

Normals are computed using GetNormal(Vector2, Vector2, bool) with the third parameter set to false. When the polygon vertices are in counter-clockwise (CCW) order the normals will face outward.

GetIncircle(int, int)

Computes an approximate incircle (largest inscribed circle) for the polygon by searching for a point inside the polygon that maximizes the distance to the nearest edge. The method uses iterative radial sampling (hill-climb) from an initial seed to refine the circle center.

public Circle GetIncircle(int iterations = 100, int samples = 100)

Parameters

iterations int

Number of outer iterations to perform. Higher values increase refinement.

samples int

Number of radial samples per iteration. Higher values increase angular resolution.

Returns

Circle

A Circle whose center is the found interior point and whose radius is the distance from that point to the closest polygon edge. For polygons with fewer than three vertices a degenerate circle is returned (zero radius or default center).

Remarks

The algorithm is heuristic and may return a suboptimal incircle for complex or highly concave polygons. Default parameters balance performance and accuracy.

IsClockwise()

Determines if the polygon's winding order is clockwise.

public bool IsClockwise()

Returns

bool

True if clockwise; otherwise, false.

IsConvex()

Determines if the polygon is convex.

public bool IsConvex()

Returns

bool

True if convex; otherwise, false.

Remarks

  • A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward."
  • A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex.

IsConvex(List<Vector2>)

Determines if a polygon defined by a list of vertices is convex.

public static bool IsConvex(List<Vector2> vertices)

Parameters

vertices List<Vector2>

The list of vertices representing the polygon.

Returns

bool

True if the polygon is convex; otherwise, false.

Remarks

  • Convex: A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. This means none of its vertices "point inward," and the polygon does not have any indentations.
  • Concave: A concave polygon has at least one interior angle greater than 180° and at least one inward-pointing indentation. A concave polygon is not necessarily self-intersecting.

MakeClockwise()

Converts the polygon's winding order to clockwise (CW).

If the polygon is in counter-clockwise (CCW) order, it will be reversed.

MakeCounterClockwise()

public void MakeCounterClockwise()

Remarks

If the polygon is in clockwise (CW) order, it will be reversed.

RemoveCollinearVertices(float)

Removes vertices that are approximately collinear with their neighboring vertices.

public void RemoveCollinearVertices(float angleThresholdDegrees = 5)

Parameters

angleThresholdDegrees float

The threshold angle in degrees used to determine collinearity. If the angle between the vectors (prev -> cur) and (cur -> next) is smaller than this threshold the current vertex is considered collinear and removed.

Remarks

  • No action is taken when the polygon has fewer than three vertices.
  • Uses IsColinearAngle(Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, float) to test collinearity.
  • Builds a temporary Points result and replaces the polygon's vertices after filtering to preserve iteration stability.

Round(int, float, float, float)

Creates rounded corners for this polygon in-place by replacing each sharp vertex with an approximated arc of points. The method mutates the polygon's vertex list.

public bool Round(int cornerPoints, float cornerStrength = 0.5, float collinearAngleThresholdDeg = 5, float distanceThreshold = 1)

Parameters

cornerPoints int

Number of points used to approximate each rounded corner. Must be greater than 0. If set to 1 a single replacement point will be used per corner.

cornerStrength float

Relative strength/size of the rounded corner in the range [0, 1]. Larger values produce a larger arc limited by adjacent edge lengths. Defaults to 0.5f.

collinearAngleThresholdDeg float

Angle threshold in degrees below which three consecutive vertices are considered collinear and the corner is left unchanged. Defaults to 5 degrees.

distanceThreshold float

Minimum adjacent edge length required to attempt rounding. If either adjacent edge is shorter than this threshold the original vertex is preserved. Defaults to 1.0f.

Returns

bool

True if rounding was applied successfully; otherwise false for invalid parameters or when no modification was performed.

Remarks

This is a heuristic geometric approximation and may produce unexpected results on highly concave or self-intersecting polygons. Use RoundCopy(int, float, float, float) for a non-mutating alternative.

RoundCopy(ref Polygon, int, float, float, float)

Attempts to produce a rounded-corner copy of this polygon and write it into copy.

public bool RoundCopy(ref Polygon copy, int cornerPoints, float cornerStrength = 0.5, float collinearAngleThresholdDeg = 5, float distanceThreshold = 1)

Parameters

copy Polygon

Reference to a Polygon that will be cleared and populated with the rounded polygon when the operation succeeds.

cornerPoints int

Number of points to use to approximate each rounded corner. Must be > 0.

cornerStrength float

Relative strength/size of the rounded corner. Expected range (0,1]. Larger values produce larger arcs. Defaults to 0.5f.

collinearAngleThresholdDeg float

Angle threshold in degrees under which three consecutive vertices are considered collinear and left unchanged. Defaults to 5f.

distanceThreshold float

Minimum adjacent edge length required to attempt rounding. If either adjacent edge is shorter than this value the original vertex is preserved. Defaults to 1f.

Returns

bool

True if rounding was applied successfully and copy contains the rounded polygon; otherwise false for invalid parameters or when no modification was performed.

Remarks

This method is a non-mutating operation with respect to the source polygon (it writes results into copy). The method performs parameter validation and will clear copy before populating it when processing occurs.

RoundCopy(int, float, float, float)

Creates a copy of this polygon with rounded corners.

public Polygon? RoundCopy(int cornerPoints, float cornerStrength = 0.5, float collinearAngleThresholdDeg = 5, float distanceThreshold = 1)

Parameters

cornerPoints int

Number of points to use to approximate each rounded corner. Must be > 0.

cornerStrength float

Relative strength/size of the rounded corner. Expected range [0, 1]. Defaults to 0.5f. Larger values produce a larger rounded arc limited by adjacent edge lengths.

collinearAngleThresholdDeg float

Angle threshold in degrees below which three consecutive vertices are considered collinear and the corner is left unchanged. Defaults to 5 degrees.

distanceThreshold float

Minimum adjacent edge length required to attempt rounding. If either adjacent edge is shorter than this threshold the original vertex is preserved. Defaults to 1.0f.

Returns

Polygon

A new Polygon containing the rounded-corner approximation, or null if the input parameters are invalid (for example: non-positive cornerPoints or cornerStrength out of range).

Remarks

The implementation clamps corner geometry so rounded arcs do not extend beyond portions of adjacent edges. If cornerPoints is 1 a single replacement point is inserted for the rounded corner. Complex or highly concave polygons may yield unexpected results since this is a geometric approximation.
